metaData.originalTitle: 为 Agent 重新设计云：Vibe Coding 平台背后的基础设施
metaData.title: Redesigning the Cloud for Agents: The Infrastructure Behind Vibe Coding Platforms
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the infrastructure challenges behind Vibe Coding platforms and introduces how Tencent Cloud CloudBase redesigns cloud infrastructure for AI Agents through Brain/Hands separation, MCP tools, multi-tenant isolation, and Serverless architecture.
metaData.summary: The article begins by citing rapid growth data from platforms like Lovable, Vercel v0, Replit, and Loopit to argue that Vibe Coding platforms have evolved from 'toys' into 'serious business,' with the core being enabling non-technical users to generate usable software through natural language. Subsequently, it breaks down the four major engineering challenges underpinning such platforms: continuous Agent operation and security isolation, backend completeness of generated applications (databases, authentication, storage, etc.), multi-tenant isolation, and cost control. To address these challenges, the article details Tencent Cloud CloudBase's solutions, with core ideas including: adopting a Brain/Hands separation architecture to decouple Agent orchestration from code execution; encapsulating backend capabilities (databases, cloud functions, etc.) into declarative interfaces directly callable by Agents via MCP tools; implementing an 'N+1 multi-tenant architecture' for user environment isolation; and leveraging full-stack Serverless for pay-per-use billing and sub-second cold starts. The article also provides comparative experimental data against traditional VM deployment, showing that the CloudBase path can increase speed by 3.8 times and reduce Token consumption by 52%. Finally, it demonstrates the practical application of this solution through two customer cases: Tencent's 'Toast' app and GenieAI (CodeBuddy), and uses the historical analogy of 'distributed electricity supply' to argue for the necessity of redesigning the cloud for Agents.

mainPoints.point: The core challenge of Vibe Coding platforms lies in infrastructure, not LLM code generation capabilities.
mainPoints.explanation: Platforms need to solve a series of engineering problems including Agent runtime, security sandbox, application backend, multi-tenant isolation, and cost control, which are crucial for determining whether the platform can scale.

mainPoints.point: CloudBase adopts a Brain/Hands separation architecture, decoupling Agent orchestration from code execution.
mainPoints.explanation: The Agent Loop handles model inference and tool calls, the Sandbox executes untrusted code, the Session records state, and sensitive operations are completed via MCP Proxy and temporary credentials, enhancing security and recoverability.

mainPoints.point: Encapsulating backend capabilities into declarative interfaces via MCP tools significantly reduces Agent Token consumption and runtime.
mainPoints.explanation: Comparative experiments show that the CloudBase path is 3.8 times faster than traditional VM deployment, with a 52% reduction in Token consumption, as Agents spend 78% of their effort on coding rather than operational tasks.

mainPoints.point: The 'N+1 multi-tenant architecture' and full-stack Serverless are key to scaling and cost control for Vibe Coding platforms.
mainPoints.explanation: The platform environment is separated from user environments, with each user having independent data and compute boundaries; Serverless enables sub-second cold starts and scaling to zero, matching the short-task, high-concurrency work pattern of Agents, with billing based on actual usage.

keyQuotes: Vibe Coding platforms appear to be AI products on the surface, but underneath they are a combined engineering feat of Agent Runtime, cloud sandbox, application backend, multi-tenant isolation, and pay-per-use billing.
When the producer of software shifts from humans to Agents, how should the cloud itself be redesigned?

The real opportunity lies in redesigning the cloud for how Agents work: a Brain/Hands separated runtime, declarative MCP tools, a one-tenant-per-environment multi-tenant model, and Serverless billing designed for long-tail applications.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: The Evolution of Agent/Skills/Teams Architectures and Principles of Technology Selection
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory of AI Agents from monolithic to multi-agent, then to Skills pluginization and Teams parallel collaboration, and, drawing on the latest research from Google and Anthropic, provides a scientific methodology for selection.

relatedArticles.title: RAG is Dead? No, Grep is Back!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the leaked source code of Claude Code, this article deeply deconstructs its abandonment of RAG and vector retrieval in favor of an LLM-driven multi-round iterative Grep search mechanism. It compares this approach with Cursor and Codex, demonstrating the feasibility and design philosophy of a zero-index solution in code search scenarios.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: Reflections on the Paradigm Shift in AI Software Engineering
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically argues from an engineering philosophy perspective that software engineering has never truly been engineered, and that large language models, as cognitive engines, fill this critical gap, proposing a complete paradigm shift from human-centered to AI-centered, closed-loop-first, and divide-and-conquer inheritance.

relatedArticles.title: What You Don't Know About Claude Code: Architecture, Governance, and Engineering Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of Claude Code's six-layer architecture and engineering practices, proposing a systematic Agent development methodology from context governance and skill design to a verification loop.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Thinking About Agentic Engineering from First Principles
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically derives six core best practices for Agentic Engineering from first principles and introduces a modular, Skill-based open-source framework, aiming to combine engineering discipline with AI capabilities to reliably improve software engineering quality under complex constraints.
